title: Extended Build and Evaluation (Lab)
summary: Students complete their solution, run it across a six-input curated test set to report an accuracy count, handle a failure gracefully with their fallback, and finish with a three-question risk check.
objectives: Complete a working solution and evaluate its outputs across several test inputs.
Handle an incorrect output gracefully and document the fix.
Run a basic risk check and confirm no personal data is used.

body: This is the finish line for your signature solution - but finishing is not just getting one right answer. Today you prove it works by running it across several test inputs and counting how many it gets right. When one fails, your fallback catches it gracefully and you document the fix. Finally you run a basic risk check: is it accurate, is it clear, and is any prompt free of personal data? A solution you can measure and defend is one people can trust.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can complete a working solution that follows my plan.
I can evaluate its outputs across several test inputs and measure accuracy.
I can handle an incorrect output gracefully using my fallback.
I can run a basic risk check and document the fix I made.

terms.definition: A small, curated group of inputs, including edge cases, used to measure how a solution performs.
The number of correct outputs out of the total tested, such as 5 out of 6.
Using the fallback so an incorrect output is caught safely, not presented as final.
A written record of the change made to correct a failure and its effect.
A quick review of accuracy, clarity, and data safety before a solution is trusted.

sections.heading: Prove it across several inputs
body: One correct answer is not proof. Run your finished solution across a **test set** of several curated inputs and count how many outputs are correct.
Report accuracy as a simple count, like 5 out of 6, so your claim is honest and checkable.

sections.heading: Handle failures and check the risks
body: When an output is wrong, let your fallback catch it and keep a person in the loop, then document the fix and its effect.
Finish with a basic risk check: accurate enough? clear enough? any personal data used? The data answer must always be no, because we use only curated inputs.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
body: You will complete your solution, evaluate it across six curated inputs, handle any failure with your fallback, document the fix, and run a basic risk check. The teacher runs the AI on the board; you do not log in.
items: Confirm your build follows the plan and the fallback is wired in.
Define what counts as a correct output.
Run all six curated inputs and record each result.
Compute accuracy and handle any failure with your fallback, documenting the fix.
Complete the three-question risk check and note the biggest remaining risk.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Why is an accuracy count across several inputs fairer than judging one output?
What is the biggest remaining risk in your solution, and who should check it?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write your accuracy result and the fix you documented.
Write one thing your risk check made you notice.

worksheet.title: Week 8 - Lab - Worksheet | Extended Build and Evaluation (Lab)

questions.prompt: Omar runs his finished solution on all six curated test inputs. Inputs 1, 2, 4 and 6 give outputs that match his agreed definition of a correct output. Input 3 gives a wrong label. Input 5 gives an output so unclear that it fails his check. What number should Omar report as his accuracy count out of 6?

feedback.correct: An output that is too unclear to pass the check counts as not correct, so Omar reports 4 out of 6.
feedback.incorrect: Only outputs that meet the definition of correct are counted - the unclear one fails the check, so the honest count is 4 out of 6.

questions.prompt: Nadia's finished solution gives a wrong label for one of her test inputs. Which action counts as handling that failure gracefully, as the lesson describes it?

options.text: Her fallback catches the output and passes it to a person to check, and she records the fix she made and its effect.
She deletes the wrong output so her log only shows results she trusts.
She reports the output as final and adds a note saying AI is sometimes wrong.
She removes that input from her test set so her accuracy count goes up.

feedback.correct: Graceful handling means the fallback catches the wrong output, a person stays in the loop, and the fix and its effect are written down.
feedback.incorrect: Deleting the output, presenting it as final or dropping the input all hide the failure - the fallback is there to catch it and pass it to a person.

questions.prompt: Rashid tells the class 'my solution is accurate' after showing one input that came out right. According to the lesson, what is his claim missing? Select all that apply.

options.text: A count across all six curated test inputs, such as 5 out of 6.
A definition of what counts as a correct output, agreed before testing.
Which of the six inputs failed, not just the total that passed.
A promise that his solution will never get an answer wrong.
The names of the classmates whose details he tested it on.

feedback.correct: An honest accuracy claim is a count across the whole curated test set, judged against a definition of correct agreed before testing, including the harder cases.
feedback.incorrect: No solution can promise it will never be wrong, and personal data never belongs in a test set - what Rashid is missing is a checkable count across all his curated inputs.

questions.prompt: Match each question in the three-question risk check to the evidence from a student's lab log that answers it.

right.text: No - every input came from my curated test set, with no names or personal details.
It matched my definition of a correct output on 5 of the 6 curated inputs.
A reader can tell what each output means without asking me to explain it.

feedback.correct: Each risk-check question is answered with evidence: a count for accuracy, a reader test for clarity, and the curated test set for data safety.
feedback.incorrect: Accuracy is answered by the count, clarity by whether a reader understands the output unaided, and the data question by the inputs being curated with no personal details.

questions.prompt: True or false: because Layla's solution scored 6 out of 6 on her curated test set, she can skip the risk check.

feedback.correct: Accuracy is only one of the three risk-check questions - clarity and the personal-data question still have to be answered before a solution is trusted.
feedback.incorrect: A perfect score on a small curated test set does not answer whether the outputs are clear or whether any personal data was used, so the risk check still has to be run.

formative.targets: Confirms a completed solution is evaluated across several inputs, handles a failure, and passes a basic risk check
formative.check: Test-set evaluation log (accuracy count) + documented fix + completed risk check
formative.successCriteria: Solution is completed, evaluated across several inputs with an accuracy count, a failure is handled gracefully, and the risk check confirms no personal data.
formative.evidence: Completed test-set log, documented fix, and risk-check sheet.
